In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of cord blood for the treatment of patients with CML is still in its infancy, but the preliminary data are promising.

the use of a combination of two or more cord blood units is an effective and safe approach to improve the outcome of patients with haematologic malignancies who receive cord blood transplants, and that the combination of two units should be considered in patients who receive a transplant from a single unit with a high risk of graft failure or delayed engraftment.

, in our experience, the use of a reduced intensity conditioning regimen in the context of a cord blood transplant for patients with advanced disease is associated with a higher rate of engraftment, lower incidence of severe acute GVHD and lower transplant-related mortality than a myeloablative conditioning regimen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that there are significant advantages to using the nonmyeloablating preparative regimen for patients who have a matched unrelated donor (MUD), but there is also a role for this preparative regimen when a patient does not have a matched donor.
we are able to identify a group of patients who are at risk for poor outcome.

it is possible to predict with a high degree of accuracy the likelihood of a successful transplant from cord blood by measuring the number of nucleated cells in the product and the number of HLA mismatches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now use cord blood as a treatment for leukemia and lymphoma.

the use of a double cord blood transplant is a viable option for patients who are unable to receive an allogenic bone marrow or peripheral blood stem cell transplant, and who have a high risk of relapse or treatment failure.

the current European LeukemiaNet (ELN) criteria for suboptimal response to TKIs may not be adequate to detect patients who are at high risk for disease progression, and that these patients may benefit from earlier treatment intervention.
